title: Stock Market Update: Industrials, Real Estate Lead Broad-Based Rally

organizations.name: real estate lead broad-based rally  industrials

text:
Industrials, Real Estate Lead Broad-Based Rally 31-Jul-18 12:55 ET Dow +174.16 at 25480.99, Nasdaq +64.54 at 7694.55, S&P +19.65 at 2821.99
[BRIEFING.COM] Wall Street got off to a bumpy start this morning, but has been rallying as of late, with tech shares looking to end a three-day slump. The major averages are hovering at session highs, with the S&P 500 up 0.8%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average higher by 0.7%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite up 1.0%.
Gains are broad-based, with nine of eleven sectors in the green. The upbeat sentiment has been helped by reports talks to avoid a full-blown trade war. The trade-sensitive industrial sector (+2.1%) is among the top-performing groups, rivaled only by the lightly-weighted real estate space (+2.2%).
Health care (+1.1%) is also 39.71, +1.12), which is up 2.9% after beating earnings and revenue estimates and issuing upbeat earnings guidance this morning. Meanwhile, in the consumer staples space (+0.3%), Procter & Gamble (PG 80.60, +0.40) is up modestly
The top-weighted technology sector is now in line with the broader market after a volatile start to the session. The group will remain in focus for the rest of the day as it attempts to end a three-session losing streak. FAANG names are all higher, including Apple (AAPL 191.80, +1.89), which will report earnings following the closing bell.
On the downside, the heavily-weighted financial sector is down 0.5%, hovering at the bottom of the sector standings. Today's loss trims the group's July gain to 5.4%, but that's still much better than the S&P 500's monthly gain of 3.8%. Telecom services (-0.1%) is the only other group in the red.
In the bond market, U.S. Treasuries are higher, pushing yields lower across the curve; the benchmark 10-yr yield is down three basis points at 2.95%. The dip in rates follows the Bank of Japan's decision to leave its ultra-loose monetary policy intact. The Fed's two-day policy meeting kicked off this morning.
